html:
Islam came to Azerbaijan with the Arab conquest of the 640s, when armies of the caliphate took the lands of Caucasian Albania and the Iranian province of Azarbaijan, which had been under the Sasanian Empire.

The Arabs ruled from Barda, which became a large trading city. Zoroastrians and Christians converted over the following centuries, while some Christian communities, such as the Udi, survived. Turkic peoples arriving from the 1000s, above all the Oghuz under the Seljuks, turned the language toward Turkic. In the 1500s the Safavids, whose dynasty came from Ardabil just south of today's border, made Shia Islam the state faith. Most Azerbaijanis today are Shia, though the state is secular.
sum: Islam came to Azerbaijan with the Arab conquest of the 640s, when armies of the caliphate took the lands of Caucasian Albania and the Iranian province of Azarbaijan, which had been under the Sasanian Empire.
